questions.prompt: When does the else block run?
choices: Only when every preceding condition was False
Only when the if was True
questions.explain: else is the catch-all for when nothing above it matched.

questions.prompt: How many branches of an if/elif/elif/else chain can run?
questions.explain: Python takes the first branch that matches and skips the rest of the chain entirely.

questions.prompt: What is wrong with writing separate ifs instead of elif?
choices: Every condition is tested, so more than one branch can run
questions.explain: Separate ifs are independent tests. If two are true, two blocks run, which is usually not what you meant.

questions.prompt: Can an elif come after an else?
choices: Only if there is one elif
questions.explain: else is the fallback, so nothing can follow it in the chain.
